evidence: src/domain/entities.ts declares TaskStatus, User, Project and Task, which make up one domain model.
src/domain/repositories.ts imports { Project, Task, TaskStatus, User } from './entities', and its interfaces (UserRepository, ProjectRepository, TaskRepository) are typed with those entities.
src/domain/repositories.ts TaskFilter.status?: TaskStatus reuses the existing union instead of redeclaring the status values.
src/domain/errors.ts declares NotFoundError, ConflictError and ValidationError. These are domain error types and do not overlap with the other files.
Graph excerpt: the infrastructure classes InMemory*Repository IMPLEMENT the domain repository interfaces, and TaskService constructor-injects them, so the abstractions are used as intended.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain module covers one concern: the core task-management domain model. entities.ts holds the data shapes (User, Project, Task, TaskStatus). repositories.ts holds the persistence ports for those entities. errors.ts holds the domain error types. repositories.ts imports its types from ./entities and does not redeclare them. For example, TaskFilter.status reuses TaskStatus instead of repeating the "todo" | "in progress" | "done" union, so the status values are defined in one place. The three error classes repeat the same small constructor pattern, but each one is a separate error type, not a duplicated domain rule. No file defines the same rule or invariant twice. No file goes around the module's own types: the repository interfaces use the entity types throughout.
